llm.summary: It helps automate browser checks, but it also directs agents to find, issue, extract, and store real account credentials in ways that need careful review.

dimensions.detail: The skill intentionally reuses visible browser sessions and includes a raw remote-debugging CDP fallback; the bundled CDP trace script also combines optional password submission with ignoreHTTPSErrors, which is disproportionate for a style-diagnosis helper.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No install-time persistence or backdoor behavior was found, but setup guidance uses unpinned npm/npx @latest packages for Playwright MCP and Playwright browser setup, which weakens reproducibility and supply-chain control.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Credential workflows require searching skill data, project memory, .env files, Vault, and GitHub secrets before browser use, then driving token-generation UI and extracting tokens; this is broad sensitive-data authority with limited per-source consent language.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Persistence is mandatory for issued or refreshed credentials and may write to keyrings, Vault, local cloud CLI config, .env, or skill data; Discord token guidance also mentions a temp file without clear permissions, cleanup, or redaction controls.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The browser-testing purpose is coherent and disclosed, but the skill also includes high-impact credential issuance, token refresh, scope expansion, secret extraction, cloud/API handoff, and credential revocation workflows across many services.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable granting this skill authority over real browser sessions and credential workflows. Before use, require explicit confirmation for each credential source searched, each token issued or revoked, each storage destination, and any cloud upload or publishing handoff; avoid command-line passwords and do not use the bundled login option against non-local HTTPS sites unless certificate validation is fixed.
llm.findings:
[TP4] unexpected: The package discloses a credential-issue topic, but the CDP trace script's optional user:password auto-login is broader than needed for closed-shadow-DOM CSS diagnosis.
[SQP-2] expected: Token and secret handling is central to the declared credential-issue workflow, but the artifacts do not provide enough controls for minimization, redaction, cleanup, or opt-out from persistence.
[SSD-3] expected: Collecting and persisting issued credentials is explicitly documented, so this is not hidden; it remains a material review concern because it centralizes reusable live credentials.
[PE3] expected: References to gh auth tokens, Docker credential material, AWS credentials, Vault, and cloud publishing credentials fit the credential-management purpose but show broad access to sensitive authentication stores.
[SDI-2] expected: Browser automation and CDP access are expected for this skill, but raw remote-debugging fallback plus local credential discovery goes beyond ordinary UI testing and should be treated as privileged.
[RP1] unexpected: Using @latest for runtime tool installation is not necessary for the skill purpose and introduces avoidable supply-chain and reproducibility risk.
[E5] expected: The aws s3 cp references are part of the documented Cloudflare R2/public-image handoff; I did not find evidence of hidden exfiltration, but destinations and contents must be user-controlled.
[TM1] expected: The Tailscale DELETE endpoint appears in a revoke workflow with exact-target verification, so this is expected high-impact mutation rather than parameter abuse by itself.
[EA2] unexpected: The scanner matched text in Don't/Do guidance that actually instructs agents to ask or verify before proceeding; I did not treat those matches as autonomous-execution evidence.
[AE1] unexpected: The referenced cdp-trace.md and credential-issue.md files were present in the workspace and inspected, so the partial-inspection signal is resolved for this review.
[T09] unexpected: The static finding is supported: scripts/cdp-trace.js can submit supplied credentials while Playwright ignores HTTPS certificate errors, creating a credential disclosure risk even though no malicious exfiltration was found.
